strengths: Comprehensive and well-engineered pipeline addressing real challenges in data-analytic agent training (data scarcity, training strategy, code stability)
Strong empirical results with DATAMIND-14B achieving 71.16% across multiple benchmarks, competitive with proprietary models
Thorough data synthesis methodology: fine-grained taxonomy (18 categories), recursive task composition, knowledge-augmented sampling, multi-stage filtering
Valuable empirical insights on self-consistency filtering, SFT-RL dynamics, and RL's limitations that are useful for the community
High-quality execution with detailed hyperparameter documentation, extensive appendices, prompts provided, and commitment to release resources
Successful demonstration that high-quality synthetic data can be competitive with much larger datasets (12K vs 2.5M examples)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (task taxonomy, self-consistency filtering, SFT-RL, DAPO) are established techniques; contribution is primarily in engineering and combination rather than methodological innovation

Marginal performance improvements over strongest baselines (71.16% vs GPT-5's 69.44%, only 1.72% difference; vs DeepSeek-V3.1's 70.58%, only 0.58% difference) with no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Evaluation methodology concerns: replaces original benchmark metrics with model-as-judge (GPT-4o-mini), no validation of judge accuracy, circular dependency in using GPT-4o-mini for both trajectory filtering and evaluation, uses BIRD validation instead of test set for convenience

Narrow scope limiting generalizability: only reasoning-oriented data analysis tasks (excludes prediction, training, visualization), only 3 benchmarks, only Qwen backbone models, model scale capped at 14B
Insufficient analysis of why DATAMIND-12K outperforms much larger datasets (2.5M examples); missing systematic ablations on dataset size impact and component contributions

Key components lack thorough ablation: no study of recursive task composition effectiveness, reward function design appears ad-hoc (no justification for thresholds 256/1024), self-consistency only tested with N=3, γ schedule not ablated

Data synthesis depends on proprietary models (DeepSeek-V3 for queries, GPT-4o-mini for judging), reducing reproducibility despite engineering efforts; 'automated' pipeline still requires manual workflow curation

Insights, while valid, are somewhat intuitive and lack depth: self-consistency superiority is expected, RL's inability to reverse model order follows from theory, findings validated empirically but without mechanistic understanding

Incomplete statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests despite small performance margins, 'three independent trials' reported but only aggregates shown without variance quantification
Reproducibility limitations: only subset of DATAMIND-12K provided during review, complex implementation details (chunked code maintenance), dependency on external proprietary services

strengths: Comprehensive systems contribution addressing real challenges (data insufficiency, training instability, code-based multi-turn rollout) with well-integrated pipeline
Thorough experimental analysis with meaningful ablations on data volume, training strategy, evaluation methodology, and filtering approaches
Practical insights about SFT-RL dynamics: revealing when SFT stabilizes vs. destabilizes training and that RL narrows but doesn't reverse model capability gaps
Strong reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, complete prompts in appendix, data contamination analysis showing ~0% overlap with benchmarks, training time specifications
Clear presentation with well-structured paper, balanced multi-benchmark evaluation (DABench, TableBench, BIRD) with good pass@3 diversity scores
Cross-validation of evaluation methodology showing 0.96 correlation between different judge models
weaknesses: Highly questionable main claims: DATAMIND-14B (71.16%) reportedly outperforms GPT-5 (69.44%) and DeepSeek-V3.1 (70.58%) by small margins (1.7% and 0.6%) without statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or error bars—these proprietary models were evaluated zero-shot without task-specific optimization, making comparison unfair

Evaluation methodology bias: model-as-judge (GPT-4o-mini) may systematically favor outputs matching DATAMIND's trained format with specific XML tags; reward function explicitly incentivizes this format, creating format-specific advantage unavailable to baselines

Unfair baseline comparisons: (1) Proprietary models not prompt-optimized for tasks, (2) Specialized baselines (SQL-R1, OmniSQL) trained on 2.5M examples but underperform despite specialization, (3) No retrained baselines on DATAMIND-12K with identical training procedure—gold standard comparison missing

Limited technical novelty: task taxonomy refines prior work; query synthesis uses standard few-shot prompting; self-consistency filtering is known technique; SFT+RL combination follows recent work—main contribution is engineering integration rather than novel methodology

Data synthesis concerns: DATAMIND-12K synthesized using very recent expert models (DeepSeek-V3); semantic overlap beyond table headers not verified; few-shot examples from existing benchmarks may introduce implicit information leakage

Incomplete analysis of surprising findings: Figure 4 shows using all non-selected trajectories outperforms con-select (contradicting filtering importance claims); Figure 8 suggests cold start dominates RL contribution—these findings deserve deeper investigation but remain largely unexplored

Training stability claims lack rigor: stability inferred from visual inspection of reward curves without statistical measures; only 3 trials mentioned with no reported confidence intervals; dynamic γ schedule appears ad-hoc without sensitivity analysis

Reproducibility gaps: DATAMIND-12K promised for release 'after double-blind review'; code link redacted; data synthesis depends on external DeepSeek API; dataset construction details scattered across appendices

Limited scope: only tabular data (CSV, Excel, SQLite); only reasoning tasks (excludes training, prediction, visualization); main experiments only on Qwen family with limited transfer validation on Llama-8B

Missing error analysis: no failure case discussion, no exploration of performance by question type, no analysis of when/why approach fails, no comparison with other concurrent data-synthesis efforts for agents
